when the request body fails schema validation\n726\t\n727\t#### Validation Rules — Registration and Password Reset\n728\t\n729\t| Field | Rule | Error message |\n730\t|-------|------|---------------|\n731\t| email | Must be a valid email format | email must be an email |\n732\t| password / new_password | Min 8 characters | password must be longer than or equal to 8 characters |\n733\t| password / new_password | Max 128 characters | password must be shorter than or equal to 128 characters |\n734\t\n735\t---\n736\t\n737\t### Authorization Matrix\n738\t\n739\t| Endpoint | Public | Authenticated | Notes |\n740\t|----------|--------|---------------|-------|\n741\t| POST /auth/register | ✓ | | |\n742\t| GET /auth/confirm-email | ✓ | | Token in query string (corrected in SI-02.17) |\n743\t| POST /auth/resend-confirmation | ✓ | | |\n744\t| POST /auth/login | ✓ | | |\n745\t| POST /auth/refresh | ✓ | | Uses refresh token, not access |\n749\t\n750\t---\n751\t\n752\t### Error Catalog\n753\t\n754\t**Error response format:** (applies to all nestjs-project HTTP endpoints from this phase onward)\n755\t```\n756\t{ statusCode: number, error: string, message: string }\n757\t```\n758\tThe `error` field carries the domain error code from the catalog (e.g., `\"EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS\"`). For validation errors, `error` is `\"VALIDATION_ERROR\"` and `message` is an array of field-level error strings.\n759\t\n760\t| Code | HTTP | Message | Trigger |\n761\t|------|------|---------|---------|\n762\t| EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS | 409 | Email is already registered | POST /auth/register with an email that exists in users table |\n763\t| INVALID_CREDENTIALS | 401 | Invalid email or password | POST /auth/login with unknown email OR wrong password (same code for both — do not reveal which) |\n764\t| EMAIL_NOT_CONFIRMED | 403 | Email not confirmed | POST /auth/login when user's `is_confirmed = false` |\n765\t| INVALID_TOKEN | 401 | Invalid or already used token | GET /auth/confirm-email, POST /auth/reset-password, or POST /auth/refresh with a token not found in DB or already consumed |\n766\t| TOKEN_EXPIRED | 401 | Token has expired | GET /auth/confirm-email, POST /auth/reset-password, or POST /auth/refresh with an expired token |\n767\t| TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED | 401 | Token reuse detected — all sessions revoked | POST /auth/refresh with an already-revoked refresh token beyond the 10s grace period |\n768\t\n769\t---\n770\t\n771\t## Dependency Map\n772\t\n773\t```\n774\tSI-02.1 (no deps)\n775\t├── SI-02.2\n776\t├── SI-02.3\n777\t│   └── SI-02.4\n778\t└── SI-02.5\n779\t\n780\tSI-02.2 + SI-02.3 + If not found, throw `InvalidCredentialsException`. Verify password with `argon2.verify()`. If invalid, throw `InvalidCredentialsException` (same error — do not reveal whether email exists). If `is_confirmed = false`, throw `EmailNotConfirmedException`. Generate JWT access token via `jwtService.sign({ sub: user.id, email: user.email }, { expiresIn: authConfig.jwtAccessExpiration })`. Return `{ access_token, refresh_token }`\n- Create `src/auth/dto/login.dto.ts` — `LoginDto` with `@IsEmail()` email and `@IsString() @IsNotEmpty()` password\n- Create `src/auth/auth.module.ts` — `AuthModule` importing `UsersModule`, `MailModule`, `JwtModule.registerAsync` (inject `authConfig.KEY`, configure `secret` and default `signOptions.expiresIn` from auth config), `TypeOrmModule.forFeature([RefreshToken, VerificationToken])`. Create an `@Public()` decorator to bypass the guard on public endpoints.\n\n**Technical actions:**\n\n- Create `src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` — `JwtAuthGuard` implementing `CanActivate`. Inject `JwtService` and `Reflector`. In `canActivate()`: check for `@Public()` metadata via reflector — if present, allow. Otherwise, extract Bearer token from `Authorization` header, call `jwtService.verifyAsync(token)`, attach decoded payload to `request.user`. Throw `UnauthorizedException` if token is missing, malformed, or invalid\n- Create `src/auth/decorators/public.decorator.ts` — `@Public()` custom decorator using `SetMetadata(IS_PUBLIC_KEY, true)`\n- Create `src/auth/decorators/current-user.decorator.ts` — `@CurrentUser()` parameter decorator that extracts `request.user` — convenience for controllers to access the authenticated user's payload\n- Register `JwtAuthGuard` as a global guard via `APP_GUARD` in `AuthModule` providers — all endpoints require authentication by default; use `@Public()` to opt out\n- Add `@Public()` to all existing auth endpoints in `AuthController` (register, confirm-email, resend-confirmation, login) and to `AppController.getHello()`\n\n**Tests:**\n\n| File | Layer | Verifies |\n|------|-------|----------|\n| `src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.spec.ts` | Unit | Valid JWT passes, expired JWT rejected, missing header rejected, `@Public()` routes bypass guard |\n| `test/auth.e2e-spec.ts` | E2E | Protected endpoint returns 401 without token, 200 with valid token; public endpoints remain accessible |\n\n**Dependencies:** SI-02.8\n\n**Acceptance criteria:**\n\n- A request to a non-public endpoint without an `Authorization` header returns 401\n- A request with an invalid or expired JWT returns 401\n- A request with a valid JWT passes the guard and `request.user` contains `{ sub, email }`\n- Endpoints decorated with `@Public()` are accessible without a token\n- Existing public auth endpoints (register, login, confirm, resend) continue to work without authentication\n\n---\n\n### SI-02.10 — Refresh Token Rotation\n\n**Description:** Implement the refresh endpoint that performs token rotation with family-based theft detection and a 10-second grace period for concurrent requests.\n\n**Technical actions:**\n\n- Implement `refresh(rawToken: string): Promise<{ access_token, refresh_token }>` in `AuthService` — hash incoming token with SHA-256, look up in `refresh_tokens`. If not found, throw `InvalidTokenException`. If expired (`expires_at < now`), throw `TokenExpiredException`. If revoked (`revoked_at IS NOT NULL`): check grace period — if `(now - revoked_at) <= 10 seconds`, find the latest non-revoked token in the same family and return a new access token paired with that token (do not create yet another token); if `(now - revoked_at) > 10 seconds`, this is reuse — revoke ALL tokens in the family (`UPDATE refresh_tokens SET revoked_at = now WHERE family = :family AND revoked_at IS NULL`), throw `TokenReuseDetectedException`. If valid: revoke current token (`revoked_at = now`), generate new JWT refresh token in the same family (same `family` UUID, new `jti`), store its SHA-256 hash in `refresh_tokens`, generate new access token, return both\n- Create `src/auth/dto/refresh-token.dto.ts` — `RefreshTokenDto` with `@IsString() @IsNotEmpty()` refresh_token\n- Add `@Public() @Post('refresh')` to `AuthController` — accepts `{ refresh_token }`, returns 200 with `{ access_token, refresh_token }`\n\n**Tests:**\n\n| File | Layer | Verifies |\n|------|-------|----------|\n| `src/auth/auth.service.spec.ts` | Unit | Refresh: valid token rotates, expired rejects, reuse within grace period returns latest token, reuse beyond grace period revokes family |\n| `src/auth/auth.service.integration-spec.ts` | Integration | Rotation persists new token and revokes old; family revocation updates all tokens in family |\n| `test/auth.e2e-spec.ts` | E2E | `POST /auth/refresh` 200 with rotated tokens, 401 on invalid/expired, 401 with `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED` on reused token |\n\n**Dependencies:** SI-02.8\n\n**Acceptance criteria:**\n\n- `POST /auth/refresh` with a valid refresh token returns 200 with new `{ access_token, refresh_token }`; the old refresh token is revoked\n- `POST /auth/refresh` with an expired refresh token returns 401 with `TOKEN_EXPIRED`\n- `POST /auth/refresh` with an already-used refresh token beyond the 10-second grace period returns 401 with `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED` and all refresh tokens in the same rotation family are revoked\n- `POST /auth/refresh` with an already-used refresh token within the 10-second grace period succeeds — returns a valid access token without triggering family revocation\n- The new refresh token belongs to the same rotation family as the original\n\n---\n\n### SI-02.11 — Logout and Session Revocation\n\n**Description:** Implement the logout endpoint that revokes all refresh tokens for the authenticated user, ending all active sessions.\n\n**Technical actions:**\n\n- Implement `logout(userId: string): Promise<void>` in `AuthService` — revoke all non-revoked refresh tokens for the user: `UPDATE refresh_tokens SET revoked_at = now WHERE user_id = :userId AND revoked_at IS NULL`\n- Add `@Post('logout')` to `AuthController` (requires authentication — no `@Public()` decorator). Extract user ID from `@CurrentUser()` decorator, call `authService.logout(userId)`, return 204 with no body\n\n**Tests:**\n\n| File | Layer | Verifies |\n|------|-------|----------|\n| `src/auth/auth.service.spec.ts` | Unit | Logout revokes all tokens for user |\n| `src/auth/auth.service.integration-spec.ts` | Integration | After logout, all user's refresh tokens have `revoked_at` set; tokens from other users are unaffected |\n| `test/auth.e2e-spec.ts` | E2E | `POST /auth/logout` 204 with valid access token, 401 without token; after logout, refresh token is invalid |\n\n**Dependencies:** SI-02.9, SI-02.10\n\n**Acceptance criteria:**\n\n- `POST /auth/logout` with a valid access token returns 204 with no response body — all refresh tokens for that user are revoked\n- `POST /auth/logout` without an access token returns 401\n- After logout, attempting to use any of the user's previous refresh tokens returns 401 with `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED` (beyond grace period) or `INVALID_TOKEN`\n- Logout does not affect refresh tokens belonging to other users\n\n---\n\n### SI-02.12 — Password Reset (Request and Execute)\n\n**Description:** Implement the forgot-password endpoint that sends a reset email with an opaque token, and the reset-password endpoint that validates the token, updates the password, and revokes all refresh tokens.\n\n**Technical actions:**\n\n- Implement `forgotPassword(email: string): Promise<void>` in `AuthService` — find user by email. If not found, return silently (do not reveal email existence). Invalidate all unused password reset tokens for this user (`used_at = now`). Generate new token via `crypto.randomBytes(32)`, store SHA-256 hash in `verification_tokens` with type `password_reset` and `expires_at = now + PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_HOURS`. Send password reset email with raw hex token\n- Implement `resetPassword(token: string, newPassword: string): Promise<void>` in `AuthService` — hash incoming token, look up in `verification_tokens` where `type = 'password_reset'`, `used_at IS NULL`, `expires_at > now`. If not found, throw `InvalidTokenException`. If expired, throw `TokenExpiredException`. Mark token as used. Hash new password with `argon2.hash()`. Update user's password. Revoke all refresh tokens for this user (reuse `logout()` logic)\n- Create `src/auth/dto/forgot-password.dto.ts` — `ForgotPasswordDto` with `@IsEmail()` email\n- Create `src/auth/dto/reset-password.dto.ts` — `ResetPasswordDto` with `@IsString() @IsNotEmpty()` token and `@IsString() @MinLength(8) @MaxLength(128)` new_password\n- Add `@Public() @Post('forgot-password')` and `@Public() @Post('reset-password')` to `AuthController` — forgot returns 204 with no body, reset returns 204 with no body\n\n**Tests:**\n\n| File | Layer | Verifies |\n|------|-------|----------|\n| `src/auth/auth.service.spec.ts` | Unit | Forgot: generates token and sends email, silent on unknown email; email | varchar | unique, not null | |\n| password | varchar | not null, `select: false` | Argon2id hash |\n| is_confirmed | boolean | not null, default `false` | Set to `true` after email confirmation |\n| created_at | timestamp | not null, auto-generated | `@CreateDateColumn` |\n| updated_at | timestamp | not null, auto-generated | `@UpdateDateColumn` |\n\n**Relations:** User → Channel (one-to-one, cascade: true)\n**Indexes:** `(email)` — unique\n\n#### Channel\n\n| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |\n|--------|------|-------------|-------|\n| id | uuid | PK, generated | |\n| name | varchar(50) | not null | Display name; initially equals nickname |\n| nickname | varchar(50) | unique, not null | URL slug derived from email prefix; only `[a-z0-9_]` |\n| description | text | nullable | Filled later by user after confirmation |\n| user_id | uuid | FK → users.id, unique, not null | Owning side of one-to-one |\n| created_at | timestamp | not null, auto-generated | |\n| updated_at | timestamp | not null, auto-generated | |\n\n**Relations:** Channel → User (one-to-one, owning side via `user_id`)\n**Indexes:** `(nickname)` — unique, `(user_id)` — unique\n\n#### RefreshToken\n\n| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |\n|--------|------|-------------|-------|\n| id | uuid | PK, generated | |\n| token_hash | varchar | not null | SHA-256 hash of the signed JWT refresh token |\n| family | uuid | not null | Groups tokens in the same rotation chain |\n| user_id | uuid | FK → users.id, not null | |\n| expires_at | timestamp | not null | |\n| revoked_at | timestamp | nullable | Set when token is rotated or revoked |\n| created_at | timestamp | not null, auto-generated | |\n\n**Relations:** RefreshToken → User (many-to-one)\n**Indexes:** `(token_hash)`, `(family, revoked_at)` — composite for rotation queries, `(user_id)` — FK\n\n#### VerificationToken\n\n| Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |\n|--------|------|-------------|-------|\n| id | uuid | PK, generated | |\n| token_hash | varchar | not null | SHA-256 hash of the raw opaque token |\n| type | enum | not null, values: `'email_confirmation'`, `'password_reset'` | PostgreSQL enum type |\n| user_id | uuid | FK → users.id, not null | |\n| expires_at | timestamp | not null | |\n| used_at | timestamp | nullable | Set when token is consumed |\n| created_at | timestamp | not null, auto-generated | |\n\n**Relations:** VerificationToken → User (many-to-one)\n**Indexes:** `(token_hash)`, `(user_id, type)` — for querying user's tokens by type\n\n---\n\n### API Contracts\n\n#### POST /auth/register (SI-02.6)\n\n**Request headers:**\n- Content-Type: application/json\n\n**Request body:**\n- email: string, required — valid email format\n- password: string, required — min 8, max 128 characters\n\n**Response 201:**\n- id: string (uuid)\n- email: string\n\n**Error responses:**\n- 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS: when the email is already registered\n- 400 validation error: when the request body fails schema validation\n\n---\n\n#### GET /auth/confirm-email (SI-02.7, corrected in SI-02.17)\n\n**Request query parameters:**\n- token: string, required — the raw hex token from the confirmation email\n\n**Response 204:** No content.\n\n**Error responses:**\n- 401 INVALID_TOKEN: when the token is not found or already used\n- 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED: when the token has expired\n- 400 validation error: when `token` query parameter is missing or empty\n\n---\n\n#### POST /auth/resend-confirmation (SI-02.7)\n\n**Request headers:**\n- Content-Type: application/json\n\n**Request body:**\n- email: string, required — valid email format\n\n**Response 204:** No content.\n\n**Error responses:**\n- 400 validation error: when the request body fails schema validation\n\n---\n\n#### POST /auth/login (SI-02.8)\n\n**Request headers:**\n- Content-Type: application/json\n\n**Request body:**\n- email: string, required — valid email format\n- password: string, required — non-empty\n\n**Response 200:**\n- access_token: string (JWT)\n- refresh_token: string (JWT)\n\n**Error responses:**\n- 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS: when email does not exist OR password is wrong (same error for both)\n- 403 EMAIL_NOT_CONFIRMED: when the user's email has not been confirmed\n- 400 validation error: when the request body fails schema validation\n\n---\n\n#### POST /auth/refresh (SI-02.10)\n\n**Request headers:**\n- Content-Type: application/json\n\n**Request body:**\n- refresh_token: string, required — the JWT refresh token\n\n**Response 200:**\n- access_token: string (JWT)\n- refresh_token: string (new JWT refresh token)\n\n**Error responses:**\n- 401 INVALID_TOKEN: when the token is not found\n- 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED: when the token has expired\n- 401 TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED: when a previously used token is reused beyond the 10s grace period (entire family revoked)\n\n---\n\n#### POST /auth/logout (SI-02.11)\n\n**Request headers:**\n- Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\n\n**Response 204:** No content.\n\n**Error responses:**\n- 401: when the access token is missing or invalid\n\n---\n\n#### POST /auth/forgot-password (SI-02.12)\n\n**Request headers:**\n- Content-Type: application/json\n\n**Request body:**\n- email: string, required — valid email format\n\n**Response 204:** No content.\n\n**Error responses:**\n- 400 validation error: when the request body fails schema validation\n\n---\n\n#### POST /auth/reset-password (SI-02.12)\n\n**Request headers:**\n- Content-Type: application/json\n\n**Request body:**\n- token: string, required — the raw hex token from the reset email\n- new_password: string, required — min 8, max 128 characters\n\n**Response 204:** No content.\n\n**Error responses:**\n- 401 INVALID_TOKEN: when the token is not found or already used\n- 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED: when the token has expired\n- 400 validation error: when the request body fails schema validation\n\n#### Validation Rules — Registration and Password Reset\n\n| Field | Rule | Error message |\n|-------|------|---------------|\n| email | Must be a valid email format | email must be an email |\n| password / new_password | Min 8 characters | password Purpose\n\nThis guide helps you decide **what to test**, at **which layer**, and **how to set up tests** for each type of artifact in `nestjs-project`. When working on a specific artifact type, read the corresponding guide in `artifacts/` for the complete recipe. Supporting references (mock strategies, file conventions, gotchas) are in `references/`.\n\nArtifact types covered: entities, services, controllers, modules, DTOs, guards, strategies, pipes, interceptors, filters, middleware. For anticipated types not yet in the project, see `artifacts/future-types.md`.\n\n## 1. Testability Foundations\n\nNestJS's DI container makes testing natural — `Test.createTestingModule()` lets you replace any provider with a mock via `useValue`, `useFactory`, or `useClass`. This is why unit tests mock at service boundaries rather than patching internal methods.\n\n**Why module compilation tests matter:** TypeScript catches type errors at compile time, but NestJS resolves dependencies at *runtime* via the DI container. A missing `imports` entry, a wrong provider token, or a forgotten `exports` array causes a runtime crash that TypeScript cannot catch. Module compilation tests (`Test.createTestingModule({ imports: [MyModule] }).compile()`) are the only way to catch DI wiring errors before production.\n\n**Mock boundary principle in NestJS terms:** Mock across module boundaries, not within. If `AuthService` depends on `UsersService`, mock `UsersService` in `AuthService`'s unit test — `UsersService` has its own tests. But use *real* `JwtModule` with test config because it's a configured library — mocking `JwtService.sign()` returning `'fake-token'` never catches a wrong secret, bad expiration, or malformed payload.\n\n**Why integration tests aren't redundant with E2E:** E2E tests prove the HTTP contract (status codes, validation wiring, response shape). Integration tests prove the *database contract* (correct queries, constraint enforcement, transaction behavior). A service that builds a wrong `WHERE` clause will pass E2E tests with mocked repositories but fail in production. Both layers are required; neither substitutes the other.\n\n**Configured dependency contracts:** When you configure a framework module (`JwtModule.register()`, `ThrottlerModule.forRoot()`, `CacheModule.register()`), that configuration is a contract. The library's tests verify its internals — they cannot verify YOUR config values. Test configured libs with real instances and test-appropriate config.\n\n**NestJS 11 + Jest 30 + ts-jest 29:** The project uses NestJS 11 with Jest 30 and ts-jest 29.2.5. Jest 30 introduces ESM-first defaults — ensure `ts-jest` transform is configured in both unit and E2E jest configs. The `@nestjs/testing` module version 11 provides `Test.createTestingModule()` with full DI support. Note that `overrideProvider()` in the test module builder is the idiomatic way to replace providers without modifying module imports.\n\n## 2. Testing Criteria\n\n### Worth testing\n\n- Services with branching logic (e.g., conditional flows for registration, login, password reset)\n- Entity constraints and defaults — unique indexes, `select: false` fields, `@CreateDateColumn` behavior, cascade rules\n- Service-to-database contracts — repository queries, TypeORM relation loading, transaction boundaries\n- Service-to-external-system contracts — local storage uploads, SMTP sends via Mailpit, queue publishing\n- Module DI wiring — every module with configured imports (`TypeOrmModule.forFeature()`, `JwtModule.register()`, `BullModule.registerQueue()`)\n- Guard authorization logic — role checks, ownership verification, token validation flows\n- Exception filter error mapping — domain exceptions to HTTP responses\n- Controller HTTP contracts — status codes, validation rejection, auth enforcement, response shape\n- DTO validation wiring — one E2E test per endpoint proving `ValidationPipe` is active\n- Security boundaries — authentication flows (JWT), rate limiting, input sanitization\n- Race conditions — concurrent video uploads, duplicate likes/subscriptions, optimistic locking\n\n### NOT worth testing\n\n- Controllers in isolation (unit tests) — they are thin delegation; test via E2E only\n- Validation decorator behavior (e.g., does `@IsEmail()` reject invalid emails?) — trust `class-validator`; one wiring test per endpoint is enough\n- Framework routing — trust NestJS `@Get()`, `@Post()` decorators work\n- TypeORM persistence mechanics — trust that `repository.save()` persists; test YOUR queries and constraints\n- Mirror tests — assertions that copy the implementation's return value\n- Static entity field existence — if a column exists in the entity, TypeORM will map it\n- Single-path service methods with no branching and no system boundary (e.g., `getHello()`)\n- Guard/pipe/filter behavior that is pure delegation to a framework feature (e.g., `AuthGuard('jwt')` with no custom logic)\n\n## 3. Feature Implementation Checklist\n\nWhen implementing a new feature, use this checklist to ensure all artifacts have appropriate test coverage:\n\n| Artifact created | Required tests | Guide |\n|---|---|---|\n| Entity (`*.entity.ts`) | Integration: constraints, defaults, `select: false` | `artifacts/entities.md` |\n| Service with branching + DB | Unit: branch logic (mock repo) + Integration: DB contract | `artifacts/services.md` |\n| Service with DB only (no branching) | Integration: DB contract | `artifacts/services.md` |\n| Service with configured lib (JWT, cache) | Unit: real lib with test config | `artifacts/services.md` |\n| Service with side-effect dep (email, storage) | Integration: real capture service (Mailpit) or local adapter | `artifacts/services.md` |\n| Module with configured imports | Unit: compilation test | `artifacts/modules.md` |\n| Controller | E2E only — do NOT write unit tests | `artifacts/controllers.md` |\n| DTO | E2E: one validation wiring test per endpoint | `artifacts/dtos.md` |\n| Guard (delegates to service for business logic) | E2E + Unit if complex internal logic | `artifacts/guards.md` |\n| Guard (simple, delegates to Passport) | E2E only | `artifacts/guards.md` |\n| Strategy (Passport) | E2E via guard | `artifacts/strategies.md` |\n| Pipe (custom transformation/validation) | Unit | `artifacts/pipes.md` |\n| Interceptor (response transform, logging) | Unit and/or E2E | `artifacts/interceptors.md` |\n| Exception Filter | Unit + E2E | `artifacts/filters.md` |\n| Middleware | E2E | `artifacts/middleware.md` |\n\n**How to use:** After implementing a feature, walk through each row. For each artifact you created or modified, read the corresponding guide and verify the tests exist.\n\n## 4. Artifact Type Testing Guide\n\nWhen creating or modifying an artifact, read the corresponding guide for the complete recipe.\n\n| Artifact Type | Pattern | Test Layer(s) | Guide |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Entities | `*.entity.ts` | Integration (real DB) | `artifacts/entities.md` |\n| Services | `*.service.ts` | Unit and/or Integration | `artifacts/services.md` |\n| Modules | `*.module.ts` | Unit (compilation) | `artifacts/modules.md` |\n| Controllers | `*.controller.ts` | E2E only | `artifacts/controllers.md` |\n| DTOs | `*.dto.ts` | E2E (validation wiring) | `artifacts/dtos.md` |\n| Guards | `*.guard.ts` | E2E or Unit+E2E | `artifacts/guards.md` |\n| Strategies | `*.strategy.ts` | E2E (via guard) | `artifacts/strategies.md` |\n| Pipes | `*.pipe.ts` | Unit | `artifacts/pipes.md` |\n| Interceptors | `*.interceptor.ts` | Unit and/or E2E | `artifacts/interceptors.md` |\n| Filters | `*.filter.ts` | Unit + E2E | `artifacts/filters.md` |\n| Middleware | `*.middleware.ts` | E2E | `artifacts/middleware.md` |\n| Future types | — | — | `artifacts/future-types.md` |\n\n## 5. Anti-patterns — Do NOT Do This\n\n- ❌ **Unit test controllers** — controllers are thin delegation layers; test via E2E only (see `artifacts/controllers.md`)\n- ❌ **Mock configured libs** (JwtService, CacheManager, ThrottlerGuard) — use real instances with test config; mocking hides configuration bugs (§1)\n- ❌ **Skip integration tests for services with DB access** — unit tests with mocked repos don't prove queries are correct (see `artifacts/services.md`)\n- ❌ **Skip module compilation tests** — TypeScript catches type errors but cannot catch DI wiring errors; a missing import only fails at runtime (see `artifacts/modules.md`)\n- ❌ **Use `repository.delete({})` for cleanup** — throws on empty criteria; use `dataSource.query('DELETE FROM table')` or `repository.clear()` (see `references/gotchas.md`)\n- ❌ **Write mirror tests** — assertions that copy the implementation's return value prove nothing (§2)\n- ❌ **Forget `afterAll(() => app.close())`** — causes Jest to hang on open handles (see `references/gotchas.md`)\n- ❌ **Mock owned services' internals** — mock at the boundary (the injected service), not internal methods; if you need to mock `private` methods, the unit is too large (see `references/mock-health-rules.md`)\n- ❌ **Skip reproducing `main.ts` global config in E2E** — `Test.createTestingModule()` does NOT execute `main.ts`; global pipes, filters, and interceptors must be applied explicitly (see `references/gotchas.md`)\n- ❌ **Test every DTO rule individually** — one E2E test per endpoint proving `ValidationPipe` rejects bad input is enough; don't test `class-validator` internals (see `artifacts/dtos.md`)\n- ❌ **Throw NestJS HTTP exceptions from services** — services throw domain exceptions; exception filters map them to HTTP responses (see `artifacts/filters.md`)\n\n## 6. E2E Terminology Note\n\nThis guide uses \"E2E\" to mean **HTTP-layer integration tests** — tests that use supertest to exercise the full request-to-response chain (routing → guards → pipes → controller → service → response). This is NOT browser-based or multi-service end-to-end testing. Industry sources may call these \"API integration tests\" or \"HTTP integration tests.\"\n\n## 7. Define `@ManyToOne(() => User)` with `@JoinColumn({ name: 'user_id' })` and `@ManyToOne(() => Channel)` with `@JoinColumn({ name: 'channel_id' })`. Add a composite `@Index(['user_id', 'channel_id'], { unique: true })` and single-column `@Index` on `user_id` and on `channel_id` (per TD-01, TD-08)\n- Generate the migration via `npm run migration:generate -- src/database/migrations/CreateSubscriptions` and review the generated SQL: confirm the `subscriptions` table, the unique index on `(user_id, channel_id)`, the secondary indexes on `user_id` and `channel_id`, and both FK constraints to `users(id)` and `channels(id)`\n- Verify the migration `down()` drops the FKs, indexes, and table in reverse order, consistent with the existing `CreateAuthTokens` migration style\n\n**Tests:**\n\n| File | Layer | Verifies |\n|------|-------|----------|\n| `src/subscriptions/entities/subscription.entity.integration-spec.ts` | Integration | Unique `(user_id, channel_id)` constraint rejects duplicates; FK to users and channels enforced; `created_at` auto-populated; two different users may follow the same channel |\n\n**Dependencies:** None\n\n**Acceptance criteria:**\n\n- `npm run migration:run` creates the `subscriptions` table with all columns, the unique index on `(user_id, channel_id)`, and indexes on `user_id` and `channel_id`\n- Inserting two subscription rows with the same `(user_id, channel_id)` fails with a unique constraint violation\n- Inserting a subscription referencing a non-existent `user_id` or `channel_id` fails with a foreign-key violation\n- A newly created subscription has `created_at` auto-populated\n\n---\n\n### SI-06.2 — Domain Exceptions and Channel Lookup\n\n**Description:** Add the three Phase 06 domain exceptions to the shared catalog and a read method on `ChannelsService` so the subscriptions feature can resolve a channel (for the 404 and self-subscription checks) without owning the `Channel` entity.\n\n**Technical actions:**\n\n- Add to `src/common/exceptions/domain.exception.ts` three concrete `DomainException` subclasses: `ChannelNotFoundException` (`CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND`, 404), `AlreadySubscribedException` (`ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED`, 409), `CannotSubscribeToOwnChannelException` (`CANNOT_SUBSCRIBE_TO_OWN_CHANNEL`, 409). The existing global `DomainExceptionFilter` maps them automatically — no filter change is needed (per TD-02, TD-04, TD-05)\n- Add `findById(channelId: string): Promise<Channel | null>` to `src/channels/channels.service.ts` — inject `@InjectRepository(Channel) private readonly channelRepository: Repository<Channel>` alongside the existing `DataSource`, and return `this.channelRepository.findOne({ where: { id: channelId } })`. This keeps the `Channel` read inside `ChannelsModule`, which already exports `ChannelsService`\n- Add the three new exception cases to `src/common/filters/domain-exception.filter.spec.ts` so each maps to the correct `{ statusCode, error, message }` shape\n\n**Tests:**\n\n| File | Layer | Verifies |\n|------|-------|----------|\n| `src/common/filters/domain-exception.filter.spec.ts` | Unit | `ChannelNotFoundException` → 404 `CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND`; `AlreadySubscribedException` → 409 `ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED`; `CannotSubscribeToOwnChannelException` → 409 `CANNOT_SUBSCRIBE_TO_OWN_CHANNEL` |\n| `src/channels/channels.service.integration-spec.ts` | Integration | `findById` returns the channel when it exists and `null` when it does not |\n\n**Dependencies:** None\n\n**Acceptance criteria:**\n\n- A service throwing `ChannelNotFoundException` produces `{ statusCode: 404, error: 'CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND', message: ... }` in the HTTP response\n- A service throwing `AlreadySubscribedException` produces `{ statusCode: 409, error: 'ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED', message: ... }`\n- A service throwing `CannotSubscribeToOwnChannelException` produces `{ statusCode: 409, error: 'CANNOT_SUBSCRIBE_TO_OWN_CHANNEL', message: ... }`\n- `ChannelsService.findById` returns the matching channel or `null` without throwing\n\n---\n\n### SI-06.3 — SubscriptionsService: Subscribe and Unsubscribe\n\n**Description:** Implement the core follow/unfollow business logic in `SubscriptionsService`, enforcing channel existence (404), self-subscription prevention (409), duplicate-subscription conflict (409), and idempotent unsubscribe (204).\n\n**Technical actions:**\n\n- Create `src/subscriptions/subscriptions.service.ts` — `SubscriptionsService` injecting `@InjectRepository(Subscription) private readonly subscriptionRepository: Repository<Subscription>` and `private readonly channelsService: ChannelsService`\n- Implement `subscribe(userId: string, channelId: string): Promise<Subscription>` — (1) load the channel via `channelsService.findById(channelId)`; if `null`, throw `ChannelNotFoundException`; (2) if `channel.user_id === userId`, throw `CannotSubscribeToOwnChannelException`; (3) if a subscription already exists for `(userId, channelId)`, throw `AlreadySubscribedException`; (4) create and save the subscription. Catch a PostgreSQL unique violation (`code '23505'` on the `(user_id, channel_id)` index) from a concurrent insert and re-throw it as `AlreadySubscribedException` (per TD-02, TD-04, TD-05)\n- Implement `unsubscribe(userId: string, channelId: string): Promise<void>` — (1) load the channel via `channelsService.findById(channelId)`; if `null`, throw `ChannelNotFoundException`; (2) `delete` the subscription matching `(user_id, channel_id)`. The delete is idempotent — when no row matches, the method still resolves with no error (per TD-03, TD-05)\n\n**Tests:**\n\n| File | Layer | Verifies |\n|------|-------|----------|\n| `src/subscriptions/subscriptions.service.spec.ts` | Unit | Subscribe: throws on missing channel, throws on own channel, throws on existing subscription, saves on happy path (mock repository + `ChannelsService`); unsubscribing again resolves without error and leaves no row\n- Unsubscribing from a non-existent channel raises `ChannelNotFoundException`\n\n---\n\n### SI-06.4 — SubscriptionsService: List Followed Channels and Subscriber Count\n\n**Description:** Implement the read side — listing the channels a user follows in a single join query (no N+1) with each channel's subscriber count embedded, and a standalone subscriber-count lookup for a channel.\n\n**Technical actions:**\n\n- Implement `listSubscriptions(userId: string): Promise<SubscriptionListItem[]>` in `SubscriptionsService` — load all of the user's subscriptions joining the `channels` table in one query (`relations: ['channel']` or a `leftJoinAndSelect`), ordered by `created_at DESC`. Define `@ManyToOne(() => User)` with `@JoinColumn({ name: 'user_id' })` and `@ManyToOne(() => Channel)` with `@JoinColumn({ name: 'channel_id' })`. Add a composite `@Index(['user_id', 'channel_id'], { unique: true })` and single-column `@Index` on `user_id` and on `channel_id` (per TD-01, TD-08)\n- Generate the migration via `npm run migration:generate -- src/database/migrations/CreateSubscriptions` and review the generated SQL: confirm the `subscriptions` table, the unique index on `(user_id, channel_id)`, the secondary indexes on `user_id` and `channel_id`, and both FK constraints to `users(id)` and `channels(id)`\n- Verify the migration `down()` drops the FKs, indexes, and table in reverse order, consistent with the existing `CreateAuthTokens` migration style\n\n**Tests:**\n\n| File | Layer | Verifies |\n|------|-------|----------|\n| `src/subscriptions/entities/subscription.entity.integration-spec.ts` | Integration | Unique `(user_id, channel_id)` constraint rejects duplicates; if `null`, throw `ChannelNotFoundException`; (2) if `channel.user_id === userId`, throw `CannotSubscribeToOwnChannelException`; (3) if a subscription already exists for `(userId, channelId)`, throw `AlreadySubscribedException`; (4) create and save the subscription. Catch a PostgreSQL unique violation (`code '23505'` on the `(user_id, channel_id)` index) from a concurrent insert and re-throw it as `AlreadySubscribedException` (per TD-02, TD-04, TD-05)\n- Implement `unsubscribe(userId: string, channelId: string): Promise<void>` — (1) load the channel via `channelsService.findById(channelId)`; if `null`, throw `ChannelNotFoundException`; (2) `delete` the subscription matching `(user_id, channel_id)`. Compute each followed channel's subscriber count with one grouped aggregate (`SELECT channel_id, COUNT(*) ... {"parentUuid":"2b3c6638-c340-4bdf-a8ed-fe617b347634","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"597bc5a9-be9f-42a2-bae6-9d588dbc74f3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0174SfmEQyUvEKXJCHjjSKmD","type":"tool_result","content":"=== artifacts dir ===\nartifacts/:\ncontrollers.md\ndtos.md\nentities.md\nfilters.md\nfuture-types.md\nguards.md\ninterceptors.md\nmiddleware.md\nmodules.md\npipes.md\nservices.md\nstrategies.md\n\nreferences/:\nexternal-systems.md\nfile-conventions.md\ngotchas.md\nmock-health-rules.md\n===== services.md =====\n> Part of the `testing-guide-nestjs-project` skill (see `../SKILL.md`).\n\n# Services (`*.service.ts`)\n\n## What to test\n\n- **Branch logic** — conditionals, permission checks, state transitions, validation rules\n- **Database contracts** — queries return expected results, constraints are respected, transactions work\n- **External system contracts** — storage uploads succeed, emails are sent via Mailpit, queue jobs are published\n- **Configured lib behavior** — JWT tokens encode correct claims, cache TTL works, throttle limits apply\n- **Error paths** — service throws correct domain exceptions for invalid states, missing resources, duplicates\n\n## Layer assignment\n\nServices are the most varied artifact type. The test layer depends on the service's characteristics:\n\n| Scenario | Unit | Integration | Why |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Branching logic only (no system boundary) | ✅ mock owned services | — | Logic can be proven in isolation |\n| DB access only (no branching) | — | ✅ real DB | No logic to unit-test; the DB contract IS the behavior |\n| Branching + DB access | ✅ mock repo (test branches) | ✅ real DB (test queries) | Unit proves logic; integration proves queries — neither substitutes the other |\n| Configured lib (JWT, cache, throttle) | ✅ real lib with test config | — | Mocking hides config bugs; use real lib with test-safe values |\n| Side-effect dep (email, storage) | — | ✅ real capture service | Mailpit captures SMTP; local filesystem for storage |\n| Branching + side-effect dep | ✅ mock the dep (test branches) | ✅ real capture service | Both layers needed |\n| Pure delegation (no branching, no boundary) | — | — | Skip — no testable behavior |\n\n**Critical rule:** A unit test that mocks a repository does NOT prove the query is correct. If a service accesses the database, it needs an integration test with a real DB — regardless of whether it also has a unit test.\n\n## Setup pattern — Unit test (branching logic)\n\n```typescript\n// auth.service.spec.ts\nimport { Test, TestingModule } from '@nestjs/testing';\nimport { AuthService } from './auth.service';\nimport { UsersService } from '../users/users.service';\nimport { JwtModule } from '@nestjs/jwt';\n\ndescribe('AuthService (unit)', () => {\n  let authService: AuthService;\n  let usersService: jest.Mocked<Partial<UsersService>>;\n\n  beforeAll(async () => {\n    usersService = {\n      findByEmail: jest.fn(),\n      create: jest.fn(),\n    };\n\n    const module: TestingModule = await Test.createTestingModule({\n      imports: [\n        JwtModule.register({ secret: 'test-secret', signOptions: { expiresIn: '1h' } }),\n      ],\n      providers: [\n        AuthService,\n        { provide: UsersService, useValue: usersService },\n      ],\n    }).compile();\n\n    authService = module.get(AuthService);\n  });\n\n  it('should throw when user not found', async () => {\n    usersService.findByEmail.mockResolvedValue(null);\n\n    await expect(authService.login('no@user.com', 'pass'))\n      .rejects.toThrow(/* domain exception */);\n  });\n\n  it('should throw when password is invalid', async () => {\n    usersService.findByEmail.mockResolvedValue({\n      id: '1', email: 'user@test.com', password: 'hashed',\n    } as any);\n\n    await expect(authService.login('user@test.com', 'wrong'))\n      .rejects.toThrow(/* domain exception */);\n  });\n});\n```\n\n**Key points:**\n- Mock **owned services** (`UsersService`) with `useValue` — they have their own tests\n- Use **real** `JwtModule` with test config — it's a configured lib; mocking hides config bugs\n- Test each branch: success path, not found, invalid credentials, duplicate, etc.\n- Mock return values with `jest.fn().mockResolvedValue()`\n\n## Setup pattern — Integration test (DB contract)\n\n```typescript\n// users.service.integration.spec.ts\nimport { Test, TestingModule } from '@nestjs/testing';\nimport { TypeOrmModule } from '@nestjs/typeorm';\nimport { DataSource } from 'typeorm';\nimport { UsersService } from './users.service';\nimport { User } from './user.entity';\n\ndescribe('UsersService (integration)', () => {\n  let service: UsersService;\n  let dataSource: DataSource;\n\n  beforeAll(async () => {\n    const module: TestingModule = await Test.createTestingModule({\n      imports: [\n        TypeOrmModule.forRoot({\n          type: 'postgres',\n          host: process.env.DB_HOST ?? 'localhost',\n          port: Number(process.env.DB_PORT ?? 5432),\n          username: process.env.DB_USERNAME ?? 'streamtube',\n          password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD ?? 'streamtube',\n          database: process.env.DB_DATABASE ?? 'streamtube',\n          entities: [User],\n          synchronize: true,\n        }),\n        TypeOrmModule.forFeature([User]),\n      ],\n      providers: [UsersService],\n    }).compile();\n\n    service = module.get(UsersService);\n    dataSource = module.get(DataSource);\n  });\n\n  afterAll(async () => {\n    await dataSource.destroy();\n  });\n\n  beforeEach(async () => {\n    await dataSource.query('DELETE FROM \"users\"');\n  });\n\n  it('should find user by email', async () => {\n    await dataSource.query(\n      `INSERT INTO \"users\" (email, password) VALUES ($1, $2)`,\n      ['test@example.com', 'hashed'],\n    );\n\n    const user = await service.findByEmail('test@example.com');\n    expect(user).toBeDefined();\n    expect(user?.email).toBe('test@example.com');\n  });\n\n  it('should throw on duplicate email', async () => {\n    await service.create({ email: 'dup@test.com', password: 'hashed' });\n\n    await expect(\n      service.create({ email: 'dup@test.com', password: 'other' }),\n    ).rejects.toThrow();\n  });\n});\n```\n\n**Key points:**\n- Use real PostgreSQL via Docker\n- Import `TypeOrmModule.forRoot()` and `TypeOrmModule.forFeature()` in the test module\n- Clean up with `dataSource.query('DELETE FROM \"table\"')` between tests\n- Test the actual queries the service makes — not mocked return values\n\n## When to skip\n\n- Services that only delegate without branching (e.g., a service that calls `repository.findOneBy()` and returns the result). The integration test for the entity/repository covers this.\n- `AppService.getHello()` — no branching, no system boundary, trivial return value\n\n## Examples from project\n\nCurrently only `AppService` exists (scaffolding — no branching, no DB → skip).\n\nWhen domain services are created:\n- **AuthService** [branching + configured lib (JWT)] → Unit: test login/register/reset branches with mocked UsersService + real JwtModule. Integration: if it directly queries the DB.\n- **UsersService** [DB access + possible branching] → Unit: test branch logic if any (mock repo). Integration: test DB queries with real PostgreSQL.\n- **VideosService** [DB + storage + queue] → Unit: test status transitions, visibility rules (mock deps). Integration: test DB queries, storage uploads (local adapter), queue publishing.\n- **CommentsService** [DB + branching for nesting] → Unit: test nesting depth validation. Integration: test nested comment queries.\n- **ChannelsService** [DB access] → Integration: test slug uniqueness, ownership queries.\n===== entities.md =====\n> Part of the `testing-guide-nestjs-project` skill (see `../SKILL.md`).\n\n# Entities (`*.entity.ts`)\n\n## What to test\n\n- **Unique constraints** — inserting duplicate values on unique columns must throw\n- **Not-null constraints** — inserting without required columns must throw\n- **Default values** — `@CreateDateColumn()`, `@UpdateDateColumn()`, default column values populate correctly\n- **`select: false` fields** — sensitive fields (passwords, tokens) are excluded from default `find` queries\n- **Cascade behavior** — `cascade: true` on relations propagates saves/deletes as expected\n- **Enum columns** — inserting invalid enum values is rejected by the database\n- **Relation integrity** — foreign key constraints prevent orphaned records; `onDelete` behavior works\n- **Column type mapping** — `jsonb`, `text[]`, and other non-trivial PostgreSQL types store/retrieve correctly\n\n## Layer assignment\n\n| Scenario | Layer | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| Any entity with constraints, defaults, or `select: false` | **Integration** (real DB) | Constraints are enforced by PostgreSQL, not TypeORM — only a real DB proves they work |\n| Entity with only basic columns, no constraints | **Skip** | Static field existence is not worth testing; TypeORM maps it automatically |\n\nEntities are **never** tested at the unit layer — they have no logic, only structure that must be validated against the real database.\n\n## Setup pattern\n\n```typescript\n// user.entity.integration.spec.ts\nimport { DataSource, Repository } from 'typeorm';\nimport { User } from './user.entity';\n\ndescribe('User entity (integration)', () => {\n  let dataSource: DataSource;\n  let userRepository: Repository<User>;\n\n  beforeAll(async () => {\n    dataSource = new DataSource({\n      type: 'postgres',\n      host: process.env.DB_HOST ?? 'localhost',\n      port: Number(process.env.DB_PORT ?? 5432),\n      username: process.env.DB_USERNAME ?? 'streamtube',\n      password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD ?? The test layer depends on the service's characteristics:\n\n| Scenario | Unit | Integration | Why |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Branching logic only (no system boundary) | ✅ mock owned services | — | Logic can be proven in isolation |\n| DB access only (no branching) | — | ✅ real DB | No logic to unit-test; the DB contract IS the behavior |\n| Branching + DB access | ✅ mock repo (test branches) | ✅ real DB (test queries) | Unit proves logic; integration proves queries — neither substitutes the other |\n| Configured lib (JWT, cache, throttle) | ✅ real lib with test config | — | Mocking hides config bugs; use real lib with test-safe values |\n| Side-effect dep (email, storage) | — | ✅ real capture service | Mailpit captures SMTP; local filesystem for storage |\n| Branching + side-effect dep | ✅ mock the dep (test branches) | ✅ real capture service | Both layers needed |\n| Pure delegation (no branching, no boundary) | — | — | Skip — no testable behavior |\n\n**Critical rule:** A unit test that mocks a repository does NOT prove the query is correct. If a service accesses the database, it needs an integration test with a real DB — regardless of whether it also has a unit test.\n\n## Setup pattern — Unit test (branching logic)\n\n```typescript\n// auth.service.spec.ts\nimport { Test, TestingModule } from '@nestjs/testing';\nimport { AuthService } from './auth.service';\nimport { UsersService } from '../users/users.service';\nimport { JwtModule } from '@nestjs/jwt';\n\ndescribe('AuthService (unit)', () => {\n  let authService: AuthService;\n  let usersService: jest.Mocked<Partial<UsersService>>;\n\n  beforeAll(async () => {\n    usersService = {\n      findByEmail: jest.fn(),\n      create: jest.fn(),\n    };\n\n    const module: TestingModule = await Test.createTestingModule({\n      imports: [\n        JwtModule.register({ secret: 'test-secret', signOptions: { expiresIn: '1h' } }),\n      ],\n      providers: [\n        AuthService,\n        { provide: UsersService, useValue: usersService },\n      ],\n    }).compile();\n\n    authService = module.get(AuthService);\n  });\n\n  it('should throw when user not found', async () => {\n    usersService.findByEmail.mockResolvedValue(null);\n\n    await expect(authService.login('no@user.com', 'pass'))\n      .rejects.toThrow(/* domain exception */);\n  });\n\n  it('should throw when password is invalid', async () => {\n    usersService.findByEmail.mockResolvedValue({\n      id: '1', email: 'user@test.com', password: 'hashed',\n    } as any);\n\n    await expect(authService.login('user@test.com', 'wrong'))\n      .rejects.toThrow(/* domain exception */);\n  });\n});\n```\n\n**Key points:**\n- Mock **owned services** (`UsersService`) with `useValue` — they have their own tests\n- Use **real** `JwtModule` with test config — it's a configured lib; The project's architecture rules enforce this (see `nestjs-layer-separation` rule). Testing what controllers do means testing the HTTP contract:\n\n- **Status codes** — correct HTTP status for each operation (200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409)\n- **Validation rejection** — `ValidationPipe` rejects invalid payloads with 400\n- **Auth enforcement** — protected routes return 401 without token, 403 without permission\n- **Response shape** — response body matches expected structure\n- **Error responses** — domain exceptions map to correct HTTP error format via exception filters\n\n## Layer assignment\n\n| Scenario | Unit | Integration | E2E |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Any controller | ❌ Never | — | ✅ Always |\n\n**Why no unit tests:** Controllers have no business logic (per project rules). A unit test for a controller that mocks the service and asserts the return value is a mirror test — it proves nothing. The existing `app.controller.spec.ts` is scaffolding from NestJS CLI and should not be used as a pattern for new controllers.\n\n## Setup pattern\n\n```typescript\n// test/users.e2e-spec.ts\nimport { In this project, services throw domain exceptions (custom Error subclasses) — filters map them to proper HTTP status codes and response bodies.\n\n- **Domain exception → HTTP mapping** — each domain exception maps to the correct status code and response format\n- **Unknown exception handling** — unexpected errors produce a generic 500 response without leaking internals\n- **Error response format** — all error responses follow a consistent structure\n\n## Layer assignment\n\n| Scenario | Unit | E2E | Why |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Custom exception filter with mapping logic | ✅ | ✅ | Unit tests mapping rules; E2E verifies wiring and real HTTP responses |\n| Filter extending `BaseExceptionFilter` with custom logic | ✅ | ✅ | Unit for the custom logic; E2E for integration with NestJS pipeline |\n\nException filters always need both unit AND E2E tests:\n- **Unit** proves the mapping logic is correct in isolation\n- **E2E** proves the filter is registered and receives exceptions from the real pipeline\n\n## Setup pattern — Unit test\n\n```typescript\n// domain-exception.filter.spec.ts\nimport { DomainExceptionFilter } from './domain-exception.filter';\nimport { {"parentUuid":"29614095-409c-4fc2-85e9-893a52941610","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"/home/guilherme/fullcycle/aluno/project-idea-with-ai/mba-ia-greenfield-project/.claude/rules/typescript-strict.md","content":{"path":"/home/guilherme/fullcycle/aluno/project-idea-with-ai/mba-ia-greenfield-project/.claude/rules/typescript-strict.md","type":"Project","content":"# TypeScript Rules\n\nThe project compiles with `strict` settings (`strictNullChecks`, etc.). `npx tsc --noEmit` must exit with code 0 before any task is considered done — never leave compilation errors as debt for a future cleanup task.\n\n## Type-Only Imports\n\nWhen an import is used **only** as a type (in annotations, generics, `extends`, `implements`), use `import type`:\n\n```typescript\nimport type { JwtPayload } from './types/jwt-payload';\nimport type { ConfigType } from '@nestjs/config';\n```\n\nThis avoids runtime imports of type-only modules (which can break with `verbatimModuleSyntax` / `isolatedModules`) and keeps the compiled output minimal.\n\nIf the same module exports both values and types, use the inline form:\n\n```typescript\nimport { someFunction, type SomeType } from './module';\n```\n\n## NestJS ConfigType\n\nWhen injecting a typed config built with `registerAs`, use `ConfigType<typeof myConfig>` from `@nestjs/config` — not `ReturnType<typeof myConfig>`:\n\n```typescript\nimport authConfig from './auth.config';\nimport type { ConfigType } from '@nestjs/config';\n\nconstructor(\n  @Inject(authConfig.KEY)\n  private readonly config: ConfigType<typeof authConfig>,\n) {}\n```\n\n`ConfigType` resolves promises returned by async factories; `ReturnType` does not.\n\n## Strict Null Defaults\n\nWhen reading optional env vars with `process.env.X` directly, narrow before use:\n\n```typescript\nconst port = parseInt(process.env.PORT ?? Always use the container for development:\n\n```bash\n# Start containers\ndocker compose up -d\n\n# Install dependencies (first time only)\ndocker compose exec nestjs-api npm install\n\n# Run the dev server (watch mode)\ndocker compose exec nestjs-api npm run start:dev\n```\n\nServices:\n- `nestjs-api` — NestJS API, port `3000`\n- `db` — PostgreSQL 17, port `5432`, database `streamtube`, user/password `streamtube`\n\nAll verification and teardown commands run on the **host machine**:\n\n```bash\n# Verify NestJS is running (expect 200 + \"Hello World!\")\ncurl http://localhost:3000\n\n# Verify PostgreSQL is ready (runs inside the db container)\ndocker compose exec db pg_isready -U streamtube\n\n# Check container logs\ndocker compose logs nestjs-api\ndocker compose logs db\n\n# Tear down the entire environment\ndocker compose down\n```\n\n## Commands\n\n**Strict rule:** every `npm`, `npx`, `node`, `tsc`, and test command runs **inside the container**, never on the host. Running on the host causes env-var divergence (`DB_HOST` resolves to `localhost` instead of the Compose service), uses a different Node version, and produces results that do not reflect what runs in CI/prod.\n\n### Container-only commands (always prefix with `docker compose exec nestjs-api`)\n\n```bash\nnpm run start:dev                        # Dev server with hot-reload\nnpm run build                            # Compile to dist/\nnpm run start:prod                       # Run compiled build\n\nnpm test                                 # Unit tests\nnpm run test:watch                       # Unit tests in watch mode\nnpm run test:cov                         # Coverage report\nnpm run test:e2e                         # End-to-end tests (always with --runInBand)\n\nnpx tsc --noEmit                         # Type-check (required before declaring a task done)\nnpm run lint                             # ESLint with auto-fix\nnpm run format                           # Prettier formatting\n```\n\n### Host-only commands (Docker / connectivity probes)\n\n```bash\ndocker compose ps\ndocker compose logs nestjs-api\ndocker compose exec db pg_isready -U streamtube\ncurl http://localhost:3000\n```\n\n### Test execution\n\nIntegration and e2e suites share a single test database. They **must** be run with `--runInBand`:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose exec nestjs-api npm test -- --runInBand\ndocker compose exec nestjs-api npm run test:e2e   # already configured\n```\n\nParallel execution causes FK violations, deadlocks, and cross-suite contamination because suites truncate or seed shared tables concurrently.\n\nDuring active development, run only the tests related to the file being changed (`npm test -- path/to/file.spec.ts`). Before declaring a task done, run the full suite — see the global `CLAUDE.md` → \"Definition of Done (Technical)\".\n\n## Long-running Processes\n\nCommands that never exit (dev server, watch modes) must be run in background in the Bash tool — otherwise the agent blocks indefinitely waiting for the process to return.\n\nThis applies to: `start:dev`, `start:prod`, `test:watch`, and any other persistent process.\n\n## Test Type Selection\n\nChoose the suffix by what the test really does, not by where the code under test lives. The suffix is a contract that drives Jest config (`testRegex`, parallelism), CI steps, and reader expectations.\n\n| Suffix                  | Purpose                                                              | DB / external I/O | Location                     |\n|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|\n| `*.spec.ts`             | **Unit** — pure logic, all collaborators mocked                      | Forbidden         | Next to the source file      |\n| `*.integration-spec.ts` | **Integration** — exercises real DB, real repositories, real modules | Required          | Next to the source file      |\n| `*.e2e-spec.ts`         | **End-to-end** — full HTTP cycle via `supertest`                     | Required          | `nestjs-project/test/`       |\n\nA test that constructs a `TypeOrmModule.forRoot`, opens a connection, or hits the `db` service **must** be `*.integration-spec.ts`, never `*.spec.ts`. A test that boots the full Nest application and makes HTTP calls **must** be `*.e2e-spec.ts`.\n\nConventions for **how to write** each kind of test (mocking patterns, AAA structure, override strategies for global guards, etc.) live in `.claude/rules/nestjs-testing.md` and load when you edit a test file.\n\n## Jest Configuration\n\nThese settings are required in `package.json` (jest config) and `test/jest-e2e.json` for the project's tests to work correctly:\n\n- `setupFiles: [\"dotenv/config\"]` — without this, `.env` is not loaded inside the Jest process. `DB_HOST`, `JWT_SECRET`, etc. fall back to undefined or to the host's `localhost`, breaking container-to-container DNS.\n- `testRegex: '.*\\\\.(spec|integration-spec)\\\\.ts$'` — covers both unit (`*.spec.ts`) and integration (`*.integration-spec.ts`) suffixes.\n\nDo not add new test-file suffixes; if a new test type is needed, update the regex deliberately.\n\n## Environment File Conventions\n\n`.env` is parsed by both Docker Compose and `dotenv` — values containing shell-special characters (`<`, `>`, `|`, `&`, spaces) **must be quoted** or rewritten:\n\n```dotenv\n# Wrong — the unquoted angle brackets are shell redirection syntax and break parsing\nMAIL_FROM=StreamTube <noreply@streamtube.local>\n\n# Right — quote the value\nMAIL_FROM=\"StreamTube <noreply@streamtube.local>\"\n```\n\nWhenever possible, prefer storing only the bare address in `.env` and composing display names in code (e.g., in `mail.config.ts`) so the file stays shell-safe.\n\n## Build Assets\n\n`tsc` (and therefore `nest build`) only emits compiled `.ts` files to `dist/`. Any non-TypeScript runtime asset — Handlebars templates (`.hbs`), JSON fixtures, static config files, etc. — must be declared in `nest-cli.json` under `compilerOptions.assets` (with `watchAssets: true` for dev). Without that, the file exists in `src/` but is missing in `dist/` and runtime fails only after build.\n\n## Architecture\n\nNestJS with standard module structure. Source lives in `src/`, compiled output in `dist/`.\n\n- Each domain feature gets its own module (e.g., `UsersModule`, `VideosModule`) registered in `AppModule`\n- Controllers handle HTTP routing; Services hold business logic; both are scoped to their module\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n- **TypeScript:** `nodenext` module resolution, `ES2023` target, `strictNullChecks` on, `noImplicitAny` off\n- **Decorators:** `emitDecoratorMetadata` + `experimentalDecorators` enabled — required for NestJS DI\n- **Prettier:** single quotes, trailing commas everywhere\n- **ESLint:** `no-explicit-any` allowed; `no-floating-promises` and `no-unsafe-argument` are warnings\n\n## REST Conventions\n\nThis is a RESTful API. TypeORM (and PostgreSQL) accept the bad code and return wrong results, which makes the bug visible only at runtime in a downstream check.\n\n## `null` in `where` is silently dropped\n\n`where: { someField: null }` does **not** generate `WHERE some_field IS NULL` — it is silently removed from the query. Use the `IsNull()` helper:\n\n```typescript\nimport { IsNull, Not } from 'typeorm';\n\nrepo.findOne({ where: { confirmedAt: IsNull() } });\nrepo.find({ where: { revokedAt: Not(IsNull()) } });\n```\n\n## PostgreSQL aborts the transaction on constraint violation\n\nWhen a query inside `dataSource.transaction(...)` (or `manager.query`/`manager.save` within a transaction) raises any error, PostgreSQL puts the transaction in an **aborted** state and refuses every subsequent statement until the transaction is rolled back. A naive retry loop inside the same transaction will fail with:\n\n```\ncurrent transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block\n```\n\nFor retry-on-collision patterns (e.g., generating a unique handle / nickname), wrap each attempt in a SAVEPOINT so only the failed attempt is rolled back:\n\n```typescript\nawait dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {\n    await manager.query(`SAVEPOINT attempt_${attempt}`);\n    try {\n      await manager.save(entity);\n      await manager.query(`RELEASE SAVEPOINT attempt_${attempt}`);\n      return;\n    } catch (err) {\n      await manager.query(`ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT attempt_${attempt}`);\n      if (!isUniqueViolation(err) || attempt === MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1) throw err;\n      // mutate the colliding field and retry\n    }\n  }\n});\n```\n\n## `findOne` vs `findOneOrFail`\n\n- `findOne` returns `null` when no row matches — caller must handle the `null` and throw a domain exception if absence is an error.\n- `findOneOrFail` throws TypeORM's `EntityNotFoundError` — only use it when the absence is genuinely exceptional and you do **not** want to convert it into a domain-specific exception. Prefer `findOne` + explicit domain exception in service code so error filters can map the response cleanly.\n\n## Selecting columns excluded with `select: false`\n\nSensitive columns declared with `{ select: false }` (passwords, tokens) are absent from default queries. To load them in flows that legitimately need them (e.g., login):\n\n```typescript\nrepo.findOne({\n  where: { email },\n  select: ['id', 'email', 'passwordHash'],\n});\n```\n\nOr use the QueryBuilder with `.addSelect('user.passwordHash')`. Every error must either:\n1. **Propagate naturally** — don't catch it at all, let it bubble up\n2. **Be re-thrown** — catch to add context or transform, then re-throw\n\nA `try/catch` that logs and returns `null`, `undefined`, `false`, or an empty value instead of throwing is a silent failure. This hides bugs and makes debugging extremely difficult.\n\n## Bad: swallowing the error\n\n```typescript\nasync findById(id: string): Promise<User | null> {\n  try {\n    return await this.userRepository.findOneByOrFail({ id });\n  } catch (error) {\n    this.logger.error('User not found', error);\n    return null; // caller has no idea something went wrong\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Good: let it propagate or re-throw with context\n\n```typescript\nasync findById(id: string): Promise<User> {\n  const user = await this.userRepository.findOneBy({ id });\n  if (!user) {\n    throw new EntityNotFoundException('User', id);\n  }\n  return user;\n}\n```\n\n## Good: catch, enrich, re-throw\n\n```typescript\nasync createChannel(dto: CreateChannelDto): Promise<Channel> {\n  try {\n    return await this.channelRepository.save(dto);\n  } catch (error) {\n    if (error.code === '23505') {\n      throw new DuplicateEntityException('Channel', 'name');\n    }\n    throw error; // unknown errors propagate as-is\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## The Rule\n\n### Request lifecycle (services invocados por controllers)\n\n- `catch` blocks must always end with a `throw` — either the original error or a more specific one\n- The only exception is when the catch is intentionally converting an error into a valid domain result (e.g., `findOneBy` returning `null` is not an error — a `try/catch` that swallows `findOneByOrFail` is)\n- Throw domain exceptions (custom `Error` subclasses) — never throw NestJS HTTP exceptions (`NotFoundException`, `ConflictException`, etc.) from services. Services must not be aware of the transport layer. Exception filters are responsible for mapping domain exceptions to HTTP responses\n- Logging inside a catch is fine, but logging is not a substitute for throwing\n\n### Background tasks, event handlers e cron jobs\n\n- In these contexts, rethrowing would crash the process. `catch` blocks should log the error and optionally queue for retry or send to a dead letter queue\n- These are the **only** contexts where catch-and-log without rethrowing is acceptable\n","globs":["nestjs-project/**/*.service.ts"],"contentDiffersFromDisk":true,"rawContent":"---\npaths:\n  - 'nestjs-project/**/*.service.ts'\ndescription: 'Service layer error handling — errors must always propagate to upper layers'\n---\n\n# Service Error Handling Rules\n\n## Never Swallow Errors\n\nServices must never catch an error and silently ignore it. {"parentUuid":"15bcb77b-ab50-44f8-8ef7-809886cd8c78","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"/home/guilherme/fullcycle/aluno/project-idea-with-ai/mba-ia-greenfield-project/.claude/rules/nestjs-modules.md","content":{"path":"/home/guilherme/fullcycle/aluno/project-idea-with-ai/mba-ia-greenfield-project/.claude/rules/nestjs-modules.md","type":"Project","content":"# NestJS Module Structure\n\n- `@Module()` property order: `imports` → `controllers` → `providers` → `exports`\n- `TypeOrmModule.forFeature([...])` goes in domain module `imports`, never in `AppModule`\n- **Every entity must be registered in `TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Entity])` of its owning module.** Even with `autoLoadEntities: true`, the entity is only discovered if some module imports it via `forFeature`. Forgetting this does not cause a clear error: the app starts, but any repository injection or query against the missing entity fails at runtime (or, worse, the entity is silently absent from migrations). When you create or move an entity, immediately update the owning module's imports.\n- `AppModule` only contains global infrastructure (ConfigModule, TypeOrmModule) and domain modules — no business providers\n- `exports` only for dependencies other modules need; don't export by default\n- When a module exposes shared infrastructure (e.g., `JwtModule.registerAsync`, repository providers), it must `exports` them — and consumer test modules must include the same registration. {"parentUuid":"6e22679a-e536-49f5-bab8-3c0767f1d85c","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"/home/guilherme/fullcycle/aluno/project-idea-with-ai/mba-ia-greenfield-project/.claude/rules/nestjs-testing.md","content":{"path":"/home/guilherme/fullcycle/aluno/project-idea-with-ai/mba-ia-greenfield-project/.claude/rules/nestjs-testing.md","type":"Project","content":"# Testing Rules\n\n> Suffix selection (`*.spec.ts` vs `*.integration-spec.ts` vs `*.e2e-spec.ts`) and test file location are pre-creation decisions covered in `nestjs-project/CLAUDE.md` → \"Test Type Selection\". The rules below assume you are already inside a test file of the correct kind.\n\n## Unit Tests (`*.spec.ts`)\n\n- Use `Test.createTestingModule()` from `@nestjs/testing` to set up the test module\n- Mock every external dependency (repositories via `getRepositoryToken`, services via `useValue`, etc.)\n- Follow the naming pattern: `describe('ClassName')` with descriptive `it('should ...')` blocks\n- A unit test that needs to \"mock the database\" by creating a real DataSource is not a unit test — convert it to `*.integration-spec.ts`\n\n## Integration Tests (`*.integration-spec.ts`)\n\n- Use `Test.createTestingModule()` from `@nestjs/testing` to set up the test module\n- Use a real database — connect to the Docker `db` service (env vars from `.env` are available inside the container)\n- **Table cleanup:** `repository.delete({})` throws `Empty criteria(s) are not allowed`. Use `dataSource.query('DELETE FROM table_name')` or `repository.clear()` to wipe tables between tests\n\n## E2E Tests (`*.e2e-spec.ts`)\n\n- Use `supertest` to make HTTP requests against the running app\n- Test complete request/response cycles including status codes, response shape, and error cases\n- Test authentication and authorization flows (valid token, invalid token, missing token)\n- Use a real test database — do not mock the database layer in e2e tests\n- **Reproduce `main.ts` global config manually:** `Test.createTestingModule()` does not execute `main.ts`. Global pipes, filters, and interceptors must be applied explicitly in `beforeAll`: `app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true }))`\n\n## Modules with `forRootAsync` + `ConfigType`\n\nWhen the module under test (or any of its imports) registers something with `MyModule.forRootAsync({ inject: [someConfig.KEY], useFactory: ... })`, the test module must include a **global** ConfigModule:\n\n```typescript\nConfigModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true, load: [someConfig] })\n```\n\n`forRootAsync`'s factory context does not inherit non-global providers, so omitting `isGlobal: true` (or trying to add `imports: [ConfigModule]` inside `forRootAsync`) leads to \"Nest can't resolve dependencies of the (?)\" errors that are easy to misdiagnose.\n\n## Overriding Global Guards / Filters Registered with `useClass`\n\n`overrideProvider(SomeGuard).useValue(...)` does **not** intercept guards registered as:\n\n```typescript\n{ provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: SomeGuard }\n```\n\nbecause `useClass` instantiates a fresh `SomeGuard`, not the provider token you overrode. Two correct strategies:\n\n1. **Override the storage / state token** the guard depends on. Example: for `@nestjs/throttler`, inject `ThrottlerStorage` (a `Symbol` token) from the test module and call `storage.clear()` in `beforeEach` of every describe block that exercises rate-limited endpoints. This isolates state without faking the guard.\n2. **Register the guard via `useExisting`** in test modules so `overrideProvider` can target it. Reserve this for cases where strategy 1 is impractical.\n\n## Mocking `dataSource.transaction(callback)`\n\nServices that use `dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => { ... })` should be unit-tested by stubbing `transaction` to invoke the callback with a mock `EntityManager`:\n\n```typescript\nconst mockManager = {\n  save: jest.fn(),\n  findOne: jest.fn(),\n  // ...the methods the service actually calls\n};\nconst mockDataSource = {\n  transaction: jest.fn((cb) => cb(mockManager)),\n};\n```\n\nFor integration tests, use the real `DataSource` and assert side effects on the actual repository.\n\n## Compensation Logic\n\nWhen a service performs a multi-step operation that has a compensating action on failure (e.g., delete the saved user if the follow-up channel creation fails), the integration test for the compensation path should `jest.spyOn` the failing collaborator to throw, and then assert that the compensating delete really ran against the DB.\n\n## Test Data\n\n- Use factories or builders to create test data objects\n- Avoid hardcoding values in tests; use variables or helper functions to generate test data\n- Use realistic data that reflects actual use cases to catch edge cases and ensure test reliability\n- Clean up test data after each test to maintain isolation and prevent side effects\n- For e2e tests, consider using a separate test database to avoid conflicts with development data\n\n## Test Structure\n\n- Follow the Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) pattern in test cases:\n  - **Arrange:** Set up the necessary preconditions and inputs\n  - **Act:** Execute the code being tested\n  - **Assert:** Verify that the outcome is as expected\n- Use descriptive test names that clearly indicate the expected behavior being tested\n- Group related tests together using `describe()` blocks for better organization and readability\n- Avoid testing multiple behaviors in a single test case; The rules below assume you are already inside a test file of the correct kind.\n\n## Unit Tests (`*.spec.ts`)\n\n- Use `Test.createTestingModule()` from `@nestjs/testing` to set up the test module\n- Mock every external dependency (repositories via `getRepositoryToken`, services via `useValue`, etc.)\n- Follow the naming pattern: `describe('ClassName')` with descriptive `it('should ...')` blocks\n- A unit test that needs to \"mock the database\" by creating a real DataSource is not a unit test — convert it to `*.integration-spec.ts`\n\n## Integration Tests (`*.integration-spec.ts`)\n\n- Use `Test.createTestingModule()` from `@nestjs/testing` to set up the test module\n- Use a real database — connect to the Docker `db` service (env vars from `.env` are available inside the container)\n- **Table cleanup:** `repository.delete({})` throws `Empty criteria(s) are not allowed`. Use `dataSource.query('DELETE FROM table_name')` or `repository.clear()` to wipe tables between tests\n\n## E2E Tests (`*.e2e-spec.ts`)\n\n- Use `supertest` to make HTTP requests against the running app\n- Test complete request/response cycles including status codes, response shape, and error cases\n- Test authentication and authorization flows (valid token, invalid token, missing token)\n- Use a real test database — do not mock the database layer in e2e tests\n- **Reproduce `main.ts` global config manually:** `Test.createTestingModule()` does not execute `main.ts`. Global pipes, filters, and interceptors must be applied explicitly in `beforeAll`: `app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true }))`\n\n## Modules with `forRootAsync` + `ConfigType`\n\nWhen the module under test (or any of its imports) registers something with `MyModule.forRootAsync({ inject: [someConfig.KEY], useFactory: ... })`, the test module must include a **global** ConfigModule:\n\n```typescript\nConfigModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true, load: [someConfig] })\n```\n\n`forRootAsync`'s factory context does not inherit non-global providers, so omitting `isGlobal: true` (or trying to add `imports: [ConfigModule]` inside `forRootAsync`) leads to \"Nest can't resolve dependencies of the (?)\" errors that are easy to misdiagnose.\n\n## Overriding Global Guards / Filters Registered with `useClass`\n\n`overrideProvider(SomeGuard).useValue(...)` does **not** intercept guards registered as:\n\n```typescript\n{ provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: SomeGuard }\n```\n\nbecause `useClass` instantiates a fresh `SomeGuard`, not the provider token you overrode. Two correct strategies:\n\n1. **Override the storage / state token** the guard depends on. Example: for `@nestjs/throttler`, inject `ThrottlerStorage` (a `Symbol` token) from the test module and call `storage.clear()` in `beforeEach` of every describe block that exercises rate-limited endpoints. This isolates state without faking the guard.\n2. **Register the guard via `useExisting`** in test modules so `overrideProvider` can target it. Reserve this for cases where strategy 1 is impractical.\n\n## Mocking `dataSource.transaction(callback)`\n\nServices that use `dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => { ... })` should be unit-tested by stubbing `transaction` to invoke the callback with a mock `EntityManager`:\n\n```typescript\nconst mockManager = {\n  save: jest.fn(),\n  findOne: jest.fn(),\n  // ...the methods the service actually calls\n};\nconst mockDataSource = {\n  transaction: jest.fn((cb) => cb(mockManager)),\n};\n```\n\nFor integration tests, use the real `DataSource` and assert side effects on the actual repository.\n\n## Compensation Logic\n\nWhen a service performs a multi-step operation that has a compensating action on failure (e.g., delete the saved user if the follow-up channel creation fails), the integration test for the compensation path should `jest.spyOn` the failing collaborator to throw, and then assert that the compensating delete really ran against the DB.\n\n## Test Data\n\n- Use factories or builders to create test data objects\n- Avoid hardcoding values in tests; use variables or helper functions to generate test data\n- Use realistic data that reflects actual use cases to catch edge cases and ensure test reliability\n- Clean up test data after each test to maintain isolation and prevent side effects\n- For e2e tests, consider using a separate test database to avoid conflicts with development data\n\n## Test Structure\n\n- Follow the Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) pattern in test cases:\n  - **Arrange:** Set up the necessary preconditions and inputs\n  - **Act:** Execute the code being tested\n  - **Assert:** Verify that the outcome is as expected\n- Use descriptive test names that clearly indicate the expected behavior being tested\n- Group related tests together using `describe()` blocks for better organization and readability\n- Avoid testing multiple behaviors in a single test case; Do **not** try to \"patch\" the schema with a new migration on top — the generated diff will be empty and TypeORM will think everything is fine while the migration table is wrong.\n\nCorrect recovery:\n\n1. Drop the orphan tables in the dev database (`DROP TABLE ... CASCADE`).\n2. Clear the `migrations` table if it has stale rows.\n3. Run `typeorm migration:generate` against the empty database — it will now produce a complete `CREATE TABLE` migration that matches the entities.\n4. Run the new migration to recreate the tables cleanly.\n\n## Migration Tests Must Restore DB State\n\nAny test that exercises the migration runner (`runMigrations` / `undoLastMigration`) leaves the database in a non-default state.
